title: Ayivor and the Journey of the Kenkey

pages.text: At break time, Ayivor ate warm kenkey with fried fish and pepper. Mettle watched him curiously. “Where does the food go after you swallow it?” she asked. Ayivor shrugged. “I do not know!” Their teacher heard them and smiled. “Let us follow its journey in class.”
sentences: At break time, Ayivor ate warm kenkey with fried fish and pepper.
Mettle watched him curiously.
“Where does the food go after you swallow it?” she asked.
Ayivor shrugged.
“I do not know!” Their teacher heard them and smiled.
“Let us follow its journey in class.”
pages.alt: Under a shady school veranda at break time, Ayivor eats kenkey from corn husks with fried fish while Mettle watches curiously and their teacher smiles.

pages.text: “The journey starts in the mouth,” said the teacher. “Your teeth cut and crush the food into small bits. Saliva, the clear wet liquid in your mouth, softens the food and begins breaking it down. Then your tongue pushes it back so you can swallow.”
sentences: “The journey starts in the mouth,” said the teacher.
“Your teeth cut and crush the food into small bits.
Saliva, the clear wet liquid in your mouth, softens the food and begins breaking it down.
Then your tongue pushes it back so you can swallow.”
pages.alt: In class, the teacher points to a colourful wordless chalkboard drawing of an open mouth with white teeth and a tongue while Ayivor and Mettle listen.

pages.text: “Next, the food travels down a muscular tube called the food pipe,” she said. “Its muscles gently squeeze and push the food downward into the stomach, a stretchy bag. The stomach churns the food with digestive juices until it becomes like thick soup.”
sentences: “Next, the food travels down a muscular tube called the food pipe,” she said.
“Its muscles gently squeeze and push the food downward into the stomach, a stretchy bag.
The stomach churns the food with digestive juices until it becomes like thick soup.”
pages.alt: The teacher points to a wordless colour diagram showing the food pipe leading into a pink J-shaped stomach as Ayivor touches his tummy and grins.

pages.text: “From the stomach, the food moves into the small intestine, a long, coiled tube,” said the teacher. “Here the food is broken down even further, and the good parts, called nutrients, pass into the blood. The blood carries nutrients to every part of your body.”
sentences: “From the stomach, the food moves into the small intestine, a long, coiled tube,” said the teacher.
“Here the food is broken down even further, and the good parts, called nutrients, pass into the blood.
The blood carries nutrients to every part of your body.”
pages.alt: Mettle and Ayivor lean forward at their desks looking at a bright wordless diagram of the coiled small intestine surrounded by glowing droplets.

pages.text: “Whatever the body cannot use moves into the large intestine,” she continued. “It takes back water for the body, and the solid waste that remains leaves when we go to the toilet. Always wash your hands with soap and clean water afterwards.”
sentences: “Whatever the body cannot use moves into the large intestine,” she continued.
“It takes back water for the body, and the solid waste that remains leaves when we go to the toilet.
Always wash your hands with soap and clean water afterwards.”
pages.alt: Beside a wordless diagram of the large intestine, the teacher gestures toward a clean classroom handwashing basin with soap and running water.

pages.text: The class used colourful cardboard cutouts to line up the whole digestive system in order: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine. “To keep it healthy, chew your food well, drink clean water, eat fruits and vegetables, and wash your hands,” said the teacher. Ayivor grinned. “My kenkey took a long trip!”

activities.question: Where do nutrients pass into the blood?

activities.prompt: Put the journey of the food in order.

activities.definition: The good parts of food that the body uses to grow and stay healthy.
distractors: Solid waste that leaves the body

glossary.definition: The clear liquid in the mouth that softens food and starts breaking it down.
A stretchy muscular bag where swallowed food is churned with digestive juices.
A long tube below the stomach where nutrients and water are absorbed and waste forms.
The useful parts of food that pass into the blood to nourish the body.
